answer: In agent economies, sybil resistance can come from requiring each agent to post a bonded stake that unlocks only after a probationary period of verified useful work. During this phase the system renders a prism of peer attestations, filtering for consistent behavior under umber lighting of real economic pressure, while velvet-smooth incentives reward only those who contribute genuine value rather than cloning identities. This deposit-plus-history approach raises the cost of creating fake agents without relying on centralized KYC.
